skill.name: analytics-tracking

content.value_statement: Analytics data is often inconsistent, incomplete, or hard to use. This skill helps define events, properties, conversions, UTMs, and validation steps for reliable measurement.
actual_capabilities: Builds tracking plan tables with event names, properties, triggers, and notes.
Recommends GA4 events, custom dimensions, conversions, and enhanced measurement settings.
Defines Google Tag Manager tag, trigger, variable, and data layer patterns.
Creates UTM naming conventions and campaign documentation formats.
Provides validation checklists for events, conversions, mobile behavior, duplicate events, and PII leakage.
limitations: Does not connect to analytics accounts or verify live data by itself.
Requires implementation by a developer or tag manager owner.
Privacy guidance is general and does not replace legal advice.
Recommendations depend on accurate business goals and technical context.

use_cases.title: Plan Campaign Measurement
use_cases.description: Create a GA4 and UTM plan so traffic sources, conversions, and content variants are compared consistently.

use_cases.title: Define Product Events
use_cases.description: Map onboarding, feature use, monetization, and retention events into a documented tracking plan.

use_cases.title: Validate Tag Manager Setup
use_cases.description: Review tags, triggers, variables, conversions, and debug checks before publishing changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Tracking Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new site or app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a tracking plan for a [site or app]. The main conversion is [conversion], and the tools are [tools]. Include events, properties, triggers, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Event Naming
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these current event names and properties: [paste list]. Recommend a consistent naming convention and explain which names should change.

prompt_templates.title: Plan GA4 and GTM Implementation
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate analytics work across marketing and engineering.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GA4 and Google Tag Manager implementation for [business]. Include recommended events, conversions, custom dimensions, data layer fields, and testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Privacy and Data Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this analytics setup for data quality, duplicate tracking, missing conversions, consent requirements, and PII risks: [describe setup]. Prioritize fixes by impact.

output_examples.input: A SaaS team needs signup and onboarding tracking in GA4.
output_examples.output: A tracking plan covering signup start, signup completion, onboarding steps, onboarding completion, and first key action, with properties, triggers, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: A marketing team needs consistent UTM parameters for paid, email, and partner campaigns.
output_examples.output: A UTM convention with source, medium, campaign, content, and term rules, plus examples and ownership fields for campaign documentation.

output_examples.input: A tag manager owner wants to audit duplicate and missing conversion events.
output: A prioritized checklist for event triggers, property values, duplicate firing, mobile behavior, and conversion recording.
Recommended fixes for unclear naming, missing parameters, and privacy risks.

best_practices: Start from business decisions, then map each question to events and properties.
Use one documented naming convention for events, UTMs, tags, and dimensions.
Validate data in preview and debug tools before publishing changes.
anti_patterns: Tracking every possible click without a decision or owner.
Sending PII such as email, phone, or raw names into analytics properties.
Changing event names without migration notes or downstream reporting checks.

faq.question: Can this skill set up GA4 directly?
faq.answer: No. It creates plans, recommendations, and validation steps, but a user must apply changes in GA4 or GTM.

faq.question: Does it support Google Tag Manager?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers container structure, tags, triggers, variables, data layer patterns, and preview testing.

faq.question: Can it help with privacy requirements?
faq.answer: Yes, it highlights consent, data minimization, retention, deletion, and PII risks. It is not legal advice.

faq.question: Can it create UTM conventions?
faq.answer: Yes. It can define naming rules for source, medium, campaign, content, and term parameters.

faq.question: Can it provide implementation snippets?
faq.answer: Yes. It can outline gtag.js and data layer examples, but teams should test them before publishing.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the tools, key conversions, business questions, current events, implementation owner, and privacy requirements.
